edges.description: Impaired perfusion of the pre-ossified tarsal navicular causes ischemic osteochondrosis and avascular necrosis of the developing bone center.
Focal ischemic bone death manifests clinically and pathologically as avascular necrosis of the tarsal navicular.
Necrotic navicular trabeculae lose mechanical integrity under midfoot weight-bearing loads, leading to sclerosis, flattening, and fragmentation.
Ischemic necrosis in the growing pediatric navicular triggers subsequent revascularization, bone remodeling, and eventual structural reconstitution.
Trabecular compaction and structural failure directly produce radiographic navicular sclerosis, flattening, and fragmentation.
Mechanical loading across the structurally compromised, osteonecrotic tarsal navicular provokes localized medial midfoot pain.
Osteochondrosis and structural compromise of the tarsal navicular are accompanied by localized soft-tissue swelling over the medial midfoot.
Painful mechanical loading through the medial longitudinal arch causes antalgic limping and difficulty bearing weight.

nodes.description: Kohler disease belongs to the pediatric foot osteochondroses, a group of self-limited conditions in which mechanical compression prior to complete ossification and reduced local blood flow disturb endochondral ossification of the developing tarsal navicular.

evidence.reference_title: [Osteochondrosis of the pediatric foot].
evidence.snippet: Osteochondrosis is a heterogeneous group of self-limiting conditions characterized by disturbance of enchondral ossification caused by a lack of circulation.

evidence.reference_title: Kohler Disease.
evidence.snippet: Although the etiology is not fully understood, it is thought to be caused by the compression of the navicular bone prior to ossification. This leads to blood flow abnormalities resulting in avascular necrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Apophysitis and Osteochondrosis: Common Causes of Pain in Growing Bones.
evidence.snippet: Other locations of osteochondrosis include the second metatarsal head (i.e., Freiberg disease), the navicular bone (i.e., Köhler bone disease), the femoral head (i.e., Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease), and the capitellum (i.e., Panner disease).

nodes.description: Vascular insufficiency within the developing tarsal navicular produces focal osteochondrosis and avascular necrosis of bone and cartilage elements, weakening the ossifying center and initiating subsequent reparative remodeling.

nodes.description: Surgery is not routine for Kohler disease, but a small refractory pediatric series reported navicular decompression with micro-circulation reconstruction after unsuccessful conservative treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical report of microsurgical treatment of Kohler's disease.
evidence.snippet: From October 2013 to July 2015, 3 children with Kohler's disease underwent navicular decompression and micro-circulation reconstruction surgery in our hospital.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical report of microsurgical treatment of Kohler's disease.
evidence.snippet: Navicular decompression and micro-circulation reconstruction surgery may quickly improve the ischemic status of navicular bone, alleviate pain symptom and enable patients to resume normal activity as soon as possible.

nodes.description: Relative rest, reduction of painful midfoot loading, and clinical monitoring are conservative first-line approaches for pediatric osteochondrosis including Kohler disease, instantiating mechanical unloading of the necrotic segment during spontaneous remodeling.

evidence.reference_title: Apophysitis and Osteochondrosis: Common Causes of Pain in Growing Bones.
evidence.snippet: Osteochondrosis generally resolves with relative rest, but close monitoring is needed to ensure resolution.

nodes.description: Short-leg walking cast immobilization provides external mechanical unloading of the midfoot and shortens symptom duration in symptomatic children while long-term navicular reconstitution remains favorable.

evidence.reference_title: Köhler Disease: Avascular Necrosis in the Child.
evidence.snippet: Long-term outcomes for Köhler disease are favorable regardless of the type of treatment, although a short period of immobilization with a short leg walking cast may reduce the duration of symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Köhler's disease of the tarsal navicular.
evidence.snippet: Whereas patients who were not treated in a short-leg cast had symptoms for an average duration of 15 months, treated patients had symptoms for less than three months.

nodes.description: Because the pediatric tarsal navicular retains robust vascular and osteogenic repair capacity, the necrotic center undergoes spontaneous revascularization, bone remodeling, and complete radiographic and functional reconstitution over months to years.

evidence.reference_title: Köhler's disease of the tarsal navicular.
evidence.snippet: Notwithstanding the decrease in morbidity with the use of a short-leg walking cast, the long-term results suggest that all of our patients eventually had spontaneous reconstitution of the navicular and excellent recovery of function.

evidence.reference_title: Kohler Disease.
evidence.snippet: Kohler disease is a self-limiting condition with an excellent prognosis. There have been no reported cases of Kohler disease developing long-term clinical or radiologic abnormalities.
